commercial-underwriting.title: Commercial Underwriting
commercial-underwriting.description: RBC’s first production agentic solution to streamline the commercial credit underwriting process

children: The commercial credit underwriting process is
complex
time-consuming
involves multiple tools
involves fragmented data sources
requires significant manual effort.
Due to this, it requires significant manual effort from financial specialists and underwriters to prepare a comprehensive credit memo
How can we enable underwriters and financial specialists to prepare more robust credit memos while reducing repetitive manual work?

An agentic AI solution that brings together specialized agents for each stage of the underwriting process, all in one place. This includes financial analysis, client summaries, industry research, appraisal document reviews, and finally credit memo generation.
This solution is integrated into an existing application that is considered the one-stop-shop for all things commercial credit.
We implemented a dynamic DAG-based
agent orchestration to manage dependencies between AI agents and run independent LLM calls to ensure proper sequencing and reduce time spent.
We implemented a database-backed queueing system to manage background tasks, manage retries in case of transient errors, and ensure reliable processing when tasks fail.

Implemented a simple markdown renderer (from scratch 😬) on the frontend to allow for full flexibility rendering and editing markdown agent output. This was due to the constraints with the current libraries at our disposal and the tech stack of the larger credit platform.
Assisted in architecting the migration from a third party AI service to native agents in collaboration with the ML research team. This involved agreeing on
API contracts and planning
changes to our backend in order to accommodate for greater flexibility with native agents.

wealth-advisor-insights.title: Wealth Management Investment Advisor Insights
wealth-advisor-insights.description: Transforming complex client financial data into actionable insights, personalized recommendations, and ranked business opportunities for wealth advisors.

children: Wealth advisors relied on quarterly spreadsheets to access client insights and identify potential business opportunities. These reports were static, quickly became outdated, and made it difficult to explore client information or prioritize opportunities efficiently.
How can we provide wealth advisors with a way to provide more timely insights and make it easier for them to take action?
A web application that brings together client information, insights, recommendations, and ranked business opportunities in one place.

Instead of relying on periodically distributed spreadsheets, advisors can access updated information, search and filter client data, explore opportunities, and export results directly from the platform.

highlights.title: Turning complex data into usable insights

children: Collaborated with the data engineering team to integrate datasets from their ETL pipelines, building SQL-based aggregation and ranking logic to surface relevant business opportunities.
Managed CI/CD pipelines and deployments for the full-stack application using GitHub Actions and OpenShift, ensuring reliable releases across frontend and backend services.

Built interactive Vue.js interfaces for exploring client insights, recommendations, and ranked opportunities, with advanced filtering, search, and export functionality. Participated in user research sessions to better understand advisor workflows and inform the user experience.
Stepped in to lead the project during the team lead's absence, coordinating development, managing priorities, and mentoring two co-op developers to keep the project moving forward.

meeting-intelligence.title: Internal Meeting Intelligence
meeting-intelligence.description: An AI-powered meeting assistant that transforms recorded conversations into transcripts, summaries, and actionable next steps.

children: Meetings often contain valuable discussions, decisions, and action items that can be difficult to capture and organize. Manually taking notes and reviewing recordings takes time, while important details can get lost or become difficult to reference later.

Meeting transcription tools already exist, but using them for internal meetings, especially those involving sensitive information, requires extensive security and compliance reviews before they can be approved..
We built an internal meeting intelligence application ourselves that allowed users to upload meeting recordings and automatically generate transcripts, AI-powered summaries, and action items.
The application brought meeting content into one accessible interface, making it easier for users to review discussions, find important information, edit the content, and follow up on next steps.
Implemented audio streaming and upload functionality to transfer meeting recordings from the frontend to backend services for processing.
Integrated webhook-based communication with downstream transcription and AI services to receive processed meeting content and make generated results available in the application.

Built and evolved the React frontend from an initial MVP into a production-ready application, developing intuitive interfaces for uploading recordings and reviewing AI-generated transcripts, summaries, and action items.

enterprise-data-platform.title: Enterprise Data Platform Website Modernization
enterprise-data-platform.description: Migrated a static marketing website into a dynamic platform, enabling real-time ticket status tracking and integration with an agent marketplace.

children: The Enterprise Data Platform team needed an internal website to communicate platform capabilities, updates, and initiatives to senior executives and stakeholders.

What began as a simple static marketing site quickly evolved as product requirements changed. Initially, the team explicitly wanted to avoid a content management system (CMS). However, as the site grew, they needed the ability to update content independently without relying on developers.
Over time, requirements expanded further to include live Jira ticket tracking and an interactive agent marketplace with search and filtering capabilities.
The challenge was to accommodate these evolving needs while keeping the site maintainable and easy to manage.
We took an iterative approach, adapting the website's architecture as its requirements evolved.

The original site was built using static Liquid templates. When the product team needed greater control over content, we introduced a lightweight, S3-backed content management approach that allowed them to update website content independently.

As requirements grew beyond what the static architecture could comfortably support, I led the migration to a React frontend with a Node.js/Express backend, enabling more dynamic functionality and integrations.
Developed a pragmatic alternative to a traditional CMS using Amazon S3 to store website content, allowing the product team to manage updates independently without introducing a full CMS.
Led the migration from Liquid templates to a React-based application, establishing a more flexible foundation for interactive features and future development.
Built interactive agent marketplace functionality that allowed users to explore available agents through search and filtering, making platform capabilities easier to discover.

apex.title: APEX
apex.description: Predicting potential system errors through log analysis

children: For businesses that rely on digital banking platforms to manage cash flow, payroll, and transfers, even a brief outage can have significant financial and operational consequences.

Site Reliability Engineers (SREs) monitor application health using tools like Dynatrace and Logstash, but identifying early warning signs among large volumes of system logs can be challenging. By the time an issue becomes obvious, it may already be affecting users.
The challenge was to move from reactive troubleshooting toward proactive error detection, giving SREs an opportunity to investigate potential failures before they escalated into outages.

As part of RBC Amplify's four-month innovation program, our team of four students (including myself) developed APEX, a machine learning-powered application designed to identify potential anomalies in system logs.
We used a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model to analyze log patterns and flag unusual activity, along with estimated severity levels to help Site Reliability Engineers prioritize investigations.
The goal wasn't to replace existing monitoring tools, but to build on the data they already provided and give engineers an earlier indication of potential problems.
Collaborated with Site Reliability Engineers to understand their monitoring workflows, identify pain points, and refine the solution based on feedback.

We designed and developed the APEX application from the ground up, creating an intuitive React interface for SREs to explore flagged anomalies, review predicted severity levels, and identify potential issues. Built the supporting Python/Flask backend to integrate machine learning predictions into the application.
Helped take the project from problem discovery through development and prototyping to a final business and technical pitch presented to senior RBC executives.
